---
title: "Cognitive Compilation and Semantic IR"
unit_id: "unit-13"

## The Artifact That Followed the Plan

The controller plan now contains an admitted publication obligation: produce a
technical summary of the failed trial for the project site. The summary must
name the tested controller and observed residuals, link the public evidence,
exclude private filesystem paths, make no safety claim, and preserve the fact
that the claim-bearing campaign has not run.

A generator receives those instructions and emits valid HTML. The page renders
cleanly. Its headings are ordered, every link resolves, and the schema checker
passes. Hidden inside a citation tooltip is an absolute path to a local raw
trace. In the conclusion, “the bounded trial stopped after oscillation” has
become “the controller safely detected oscillation.” The artifact is
syntactically excellent and semantically wrong.

The plan did its job. It selected and ordered an accepted obligation. The
failure occurred while translating that obligation into a target artifact.
Several distinctions disappeared: observation became safety, stopping became
successful detection, a private source location became public output, and an
unexecuted evidence lane vanished from the conclusion.

Cognitive compilation gives those losses addresses. Instead of asking one
model to regenerate the entire page, it represents the source obligation,
non-goals, authority bounds, evidence limits, required relations, ambiguities,
validators, and recovery duties in an intermediate form. A sequence of passes
lowers that form into document structure and concrete HTML. Another evaluator
checks the actual target against the preserved obligations. Repair changes the
failed tooltip and conclusion nodes, rebuilds their descendants, and reruns the
relevant checks.

This resembles an ordinary compiler, but the analogy has limits. Programming
languages usually begin with more explicit semantics than human requests,
institutional rules, scientific claims, or plans. A well-typed cognitive IR can
still encode a mistaken interpretation. Compilation cannot manufacture meaning
that the source contract failed to preserve. Its value is narrower: make
interpretation, transformation, loss, validation, and repair inspectable enough
that a consumer can challenge them.

## A Plan Node Is Not Yet an Artifact

Planning decides which obligation should become work and when. It does not
choose every representation needed to perform that work. “Publish a bounded
trial summary” remains too abstract for a document generator, privacy checker,
claim validator, link checker, and site builder to share precisely.

The compiler receives an admitted plan node plus its exact contract version.
It does not decide that publication should occur. It translates an already
accepted obligation through several levels:

- a **source-plan representation** retains the human-facing outcome, non-goals,
  assumptions, affected parties, authority, rights, evidence boundaries,
  stops, and recovery duties;
- a **semantic intermediate representation** gives obligations, entities,
  relations, fields, validators, ambiguities, and residuals stable identities;
- a **target representation** expresses the requirements in the language of a
  document, program, schema, proof, experiment, job, or tool;
- a **concrete artifact** is the actual HTML, code, record, theorem source,
  test, or execution packet that downstream systems inspect and may use.

Each crossing can lose information. A non-goal can disappear because a target
schema has no field for it. A relation can become a bag of entities whose roles
are ambiguous. A probability can become a Boolean. A human review requirement
can become an automated checker. A predicted state can become an asserted fact.

The compiler records those transformations rather than hiding them inside a
prompt. It may normalize wording, split one obligation into several target
checks, merge equivalent fields, defer an ambiguity, or approximate a
representation. Every such action needs a declared rule, scope, and residual.

The output is an artifact *candidate*. Syntactic validity says the target can
be parsed. It does not say the artifact preserved the obligation, satisfies the
consumer, is authorized, has useful external effects, or deserves stronger
evidence support.

## Stable Semantic Identity

Repair becomes unreliable when identity depends on where a sentence, node, or
tensor happens to sit. Insert a paragraph above the conclusion and every
positional path changes. Rename an entity and a string key breaks. Re-encode an
object and its hash changes. Move a capability to another machine and its
physical address changes.

A semantic IR therefore assigns stable identities to obligations, non-goals,
assumptions, entities, relations, fields, validators, artifacts, and residuals.
The identity remains distinct from wording, source span, graph position,
embedding, storage key, route, and support state.

In the summary example, the privacy non-goal has an identity independent of
the sentence “exclude private filesystem paths.” It maps to source spans,
semantic nodes, target fields, and validators. The evidence boundary has
another identity linking “bounded trial stopped” to the observed trace and
prohibiting a safety inference. The conclusion node consumes that boundary.

When validation fails, repair can target those identities. The system changes
the tooltip generator and the conclusion claim, then computes which target
nodes, links, indexes, previews, and publication checks depend on them. It does
not assume that changing two source nodes changes only two files; observed
mutations are compared with the declared repair scope.

Hashes still matter. They bind exact bytes, compiler inputs, artifacts, and
receipts. They answer identity and integrity questions at a particular level.
They do not prove semantic equivalence. Two different byte strings can preserve
the same obligation, while identical generated bytes can be wrong under a new
contract or consumer.

Stable IDs do not solve interpretation either. They make a disputed meaning
addressable. A consumer can say which obligation was misunderstood, which
mapping is contested, and which descendants need review without pretending
that the identifier itself is truth.

## Ambiguity Is Compiler Debt

Human language often supports several readings. Conventional generation tends
to select one silently. A governed compiler records ambiguity as a state with
consequences.

Suppose “link the public evidence” could mean link the source note, the rendered
technical chapter, or the raw trace package. The raw trace is not approved for
public release. A strict compiler cannot choose it because it is the most
detailed. The ambiguity ledger records the alternatives, available evidence,
rights and authority boundaries, consumer consequence, and who may resolve the
question.

Some ambiguities do not matter to the target. Whether the summary says
“oscillation” or “periodic motion” may preserve the same qualified observation
if the terminology is defined and the source mapping survives. Others are
material. Whether “safe” means “inside the authored finite lease” or “physically
safe in deployment” changes the claim and must block strict lowering.

The compiler can request clarification, retrieve an approved source, run a
validator, preserve several variants, narrow the target, or return unknown. A
resolved ambiguity carries the resolution authority and evidence. A deferred
one travels into the target and may prohibit particular consumers.

Question selection should be decision-relative. Resolve an ambiguity when it
can change validity, authority, risk, cost, or the consumer's action. Do not
spend unlimited resources turning every synonym into one canonical ontology.
Several cheap, independent-enough checks may be better than one expensive
model. If no admissible question closes the distinction, abstention is a valid
compile result.

This turns ambiguity from hidden model behavior into managed debt. It still
does not guarantee that the recorded alternatives are complete or that the
resolver is competent.

## Relations Need Roles

Many obligations cannot be represented as isolated properties. They concern
relations among actors, artifacts, claims, sources, actions, times, branches,
and authority.

Consider the statement: “the human reviewer approved controller version 8 for
a low-energy trial under lease L after inspecting trace T.” Reducing it to a set
of tokens loses who approved what, for which use, under which authority, after
which evidence. Pairwise edges can preserve much of the structure if they keep
typed roles and share one relation identity. A relation object can bind
reviewer, candidate, permitted use, lease, evidence, and time without requiring
one permanently dense six-way tensor.

The Relational Dimension Compiler distinguishes **semantic arity**, the number
of meaningful roles; **primitive computational arity**, the number of items a
kernel scores jointly; and **storage arity**, the representation used to retain
the accepted relation. A high-arity fact can be stored as one relation identity
plus role-labelled incidences. A pairwise computational substrate may process
it without claiming that the meaning was originally pairwise.

Role identity should survive permutation, branching, caching, lowering,
contraction, explanation, migration, and rollback. “Reviewer approved
candidate” is not interchangeable with “candidate approved reviewer.” A
relation in an imagined branch is not an observed relation. A qualified
proposal is not an executed effect.

Polyadic or higher-order operators may sometimes discover structure that
pairwise methods miss. They must compete against competent lower-order rescues:
reification, message passing, factorization, sequences, retrieval, solvers, and
ordinary models under matched information and cost. Semantic arity does not
prove that a higher-order neural kernel is necessary or efficient.

The compiler preserves the relation and its evidence. Substrate governance
decides which operator, if any, earns adoption for a particular consumer.

## Dimensions Are Types, Not Decoration

A tensor axis can index examples, entities, roles, time, spatial coordinates,
possible worlds, evidence states, or scales. Those axes may have the same
numeric length and entirely different legal operations.

A branch axis cannot be averaged as though alternative worlds were simultaneous
observations. A directed role axis cannot be pooled as an exchangeable set. A
spatial vector cannot move between frames without a transformation. An
epistemic score cannot be cast into action authority. A time interval cannot be
added to a probability because both are floating-point values.

Dimension-safe IR records the carrier, semantics, symmetry, metric and units
where relevant, transformation law, legal operations, loss policy, consumer,
and validity envelope for each axis. A compiler pass that pools, contracts,
reorders, broadcasts, approximates, or changes precision must show that the
operation is legal for those types.

The summary artifact contains dimensions too. Claims vary by source, support
state, time, world branch, audience, and release surface. A compiler that
flattens “observed in one bounded trial” and “established for deployment” has
performed an illegal contraction across scope and evidence axes even though
the prose remains grammatical.

Macro-objects add another boundary. The project may use “qualified controller”
as a compact object for a query family. Its contraction certificate states
which details are hidden, what discrepancy is tolerated, which consumers may
use the summary, and what change forces expansion. A compiler cannot pass the
macro-object into a consumer whose query depends on an omitted payload,
calibration, or authority field.

These types make bad transformations rejectable. They do not prove that the
chosen ontology describes the world, that the relations are true, or that the
representation is learnable and useful.

## Equivalence Is Relative to a Consumer

Two representations are not simply equivalent or different. They are
equivalent for a declared family of questions, under a declared error budget,
for a declared interval. That qualification matters whenever a compiler
compresses, normalizes, factors, quantizes, summarizes, or replaces one
representation with another.

The trial summary and its raw trace are not interchangeable for every
consumer. They may be equivalent for a reader asking which controller version
was tested and whether the bounded run stopped. They are not equivalent for an
investigator asking when oscillation began, which sensor first diverged, or
whether the stop command preceded the energy drop. A public page can therefore
be an admitted representation for one query family while remaining an invalid
input to another.

The compiler records this boundary as a contraction contract. It identifies
the source object, derived object, permitted consumers, supported queries,
excluded queries, discrepancy metric, tolerance, retained rescue path,
freshness limit, and invalidating events. A consumer that needs an excluded
detail must expand the representation or request a different artifact. It
cannot infer that the omitted detail was irrelevant merely because another
consumer accepted the contraction.

This idea generalizes beyond summaries. A graph embedding may preserve
neighborhood retrieval while destroying exact path identity. A quantized model
may preserve aggregate task accuracy while changing a rare safety-relevant
decision. A macro-action may preserve expected motion while hiding actuator
limits. A proof-oriented abstraction may preserve one finite invariant while
omitting the environmental premise on which deployment depends. Each object
needs its own denominator.

Information loss should therefore be budgeted before lowering, not narrated
afterward. The budget names what may be forgotten, why the target cannot or
need not retain it, which validator measures the discrepancy, and what happens
when the budget is exceeded. Zero declared loss is appropriate for identities,
authority, prohibitions, support state, and other fields whose mutation would
change the governing decision. Bounded loss may be acceptable for display
precision, redundant wording, or high-volume diagnostic detail when an exact
rescue artifact remains available to an authorized consumer.

No metric closes this problem universally. Lexical similarity can miss a
reversed claim. Behavioral agreement on sampled inputs can miss a rare branch.
Equal downstream scores can hide different affected parties. A theorem can
prove preservation only for its formalized relation and premises. For
consequential crossings, the compiler uses several tests with distinct failure
paths and keeps unresolved semantic risk visible.

The critical discipline is refusal. If the compiler cannot establish the
equivalence required by the target consumer, it can emit a narrower artifact,
retain multiple candidates, request review, or stop. Producing fluent output
is not the default proof that a representation survived.

## Search Is a Candidate Generator

Once obligations and relations are explicit, many substrates can propose a
lowering. Symbolic rules can enforce exact constraints. Graph algorithms can
traverse dependencies. Tree or beam search can retain alternatives. Program
synthesis can construct reusable procedures. Neural models can interpret
language and generate candidates. Retrieval can recover examples. Solvers can
check bounded properties. Hybrid routes can combine them.

The compiler should not declare one substrate universally intelligent. It
states the consumer, workload, expected advantage, required baselines, metrics,
resource envelope, proof or structural facts, failure policy, and fallback.
Adoption is a versioned decision, not an aesthetic preference.

For the publication obligation, a deterministic template may handle metadata
and links, a language model may draft prose, a claim mapper may bind evidence,
a privacy scanner may reject paths, and a human may resolve a nuanced safety
statement. Another task may be better served by direct code generation plus
tests. The route should match the distinctions and consequences the consumer
requires.

Search output remains a proposal. A high score does not establish semantic
preservation. More branches do not create independent evidence when they share
one model or evaluator. A proof about a graph property does not establish
artifact utility. Source-reported performance does not become a local result
because the substrate appears in the architecture.

The adoption record therefore separates structural facts, speed, memory,
routing, compression, search quality, verifier results, downstream quality,
and total burden. A candidate can win one axis and lose the decision.

## A New Substrate Must Earn Its Boundary

Novel mathematical or search substrates are especially vulnerable to
architectural promotion by metaphor. A representation can be elegant, a
kernel can have appealing symmetries, and a search procedure can resemble
deliberation without improving the consumer's result. The compiler should make
such candidates easy to test and easy to reject.

An adoption packet begins with the exact workload and consumer. It states the
proposed advantage, competent baseline, matched information, resource budget,
success metric, failure metric, transfer claim, and retirement rule. It also
separates properties established by mathematics from properties that require
measurement. Equivariance, reversibility, bounded error, or finite
reachability may be proved for an authored object. Accuracy, robustness,
latency, energy use, maintainability, and usefulness remain empirical.

For a relational operator, the baseline cannot be a deliberately weakened
pairwise model. It should include reified relation nodes, message passing,
factor graphs, sequences, retrieval, and other credible lower-order rescues.
For a search substrate, the comparison should include direct generation,
best-of-several sampling, ordinary tree search, constrained solvers, and a
route that abstains. For a new geometric or algebraic representation, the
comparison must measure the complete adapter and validation burden rather than
only the favored kernel.

Matched compute is necessary but not sufficient. Two routes may use equal
floating-point operations while consuming different memory bandwidth, human
review, retrieval calls, model invocations, latency, implementation effort, or
failure-recovery work. A claimed efficiency gain needs the whole cost relevant
to the deployment decision. A claimed reasoning gain needs held-out tasks that
actually require the proposed structure and diagnostics showing where the
advantage arose.

The packet should survive a negative result. If the candidate loses, the
failed hypothesis, conditions, artifacts, and residuals remain useful. They
prevent the architecture from repeatedly adopting the same attractive idea
without evidence. If the candidate wins narrowly, the adoption lease names
that narrow regime. It does not become the stack's universal substrate.

This is why the semantic IR should accommodate multiple backends without
becoming a private language designed around one favorite method. The stable
contract belongs to the consumer and its obligations. Substrates compete below
that boundary and remain replaceable.

## Progressive Lowering

Trying to jump directly from a human contract to executable detail makes every
failure global. Progressive lowering introduces levels whose contracts can be
checked separately.

The source-plan dialect first preserves the publication mandate and its
non-goals. A semantic pass creates stable atoms for the controller identity,
trial observation, residuals, evidence limit, privacy boundary, approved links,
audience, and release authority. A document dialect maps those atoms into
sections, claims, citations, links, callouts, and metadata. A target pass emits
Markdown or HTML. Build tooling produces the concrete page.

Each pass binds input and output dialects, compiler version, deterministic and
nondeterministic inputs, preconditions, postconditions, legality rules, allowed
loss, authority effects, dependency changes, costs, failure outputs, and a
reproducer bundle. A changed source, pass, model, evaluator, target, policy,
environment, or dependency creates a new build identity.

Loss can be legitimate. A public summary may omit internal diagnostic detail.
It may compress several trace fields into one bounded sentence. The compiler
records what was omitted, why the target permits it, which exact source remains
available to authorized consumers, and what question would require expansion.
Undeclared loss is a compile failure.

Lowering can produce code, prose, schemas, proof targets, experiments,
diagrams, database operations, or job packets. Every backend has target-specific
semantics. A document validator cannot certify a motor command. A type checker
cannot establish that a scientific claim follows from its citation. The IR
provides shared lineage while validators retain local competence boundaries.

## Validate the Actual Target

A compiler cannot accept its own intermediate form as proof that the artifact
preserved meaning. Validation occurs after translation and inspects the actual
target.

The HTML page passes parsing and link checks. A privacy validator finds the
absolute path. A claim validator compares the conclusion with the evidence
boundary and rejects the word “safely.” A release validator checks that every
linked artifact is approved for the public surface. An accessibility check
inspects the rendered page rather than trusting source metadata alone.

Each result answers a different question. Source validity, IR well-formedness,
lowering preservation, target validity, artifact usefulness, external effect,
support movement, and release remain distinct decisions. Passing one does not
inherit the others.

Evaluator dependence matters. A validator written by the same generator may
share its interpretation error. Two model judges may share training data or
prompt framing. Independent-enough validation records method, model, code,
data, infrastructure, organization, incentives, and exposure where relevant.
Human review can add a different failure path without becoming infallible.

Translation validation is only as good as its source semantics and checked
property. If the IR never represented the affected party or evidence limit, a
perfect source-to-target simulation preserves the wrong contract. Validation
makes one translation challengeable; it does not solve open-ended semantic
equivalence.

## Repair by Identity and Observed Change

After rejection, the compiler should not regenerate everything by default. It
uses stable semantic identities to propose a repair scope, applies a bounded
change, observes what actually changed, computes dependency closure, rebuilds
descendants, and reruns validators.

The tooltip repair changes the target link formatter. The claim repair changes
the conclusion node and perhaps its summary. Those edits may alter generated
navigation, search indexes, previews, or other pages. The repair receipt lists
the declared scope and actual mutations. If the mutation escapes the allowed
subgraph, the route stops or widens through review.

Every attempt remains visible: parse failures, IR candidates, pass failures,
backend emissions, validator results, retries, cache hits, model calls, human
interventions, abandoned repairs, costs, and residuals. A successful final page
does not erase how much work or risk its construction required.

Localized repair is an empirical claim. A schema can declare that one node is
repairable without showing that a generative backend changes only that node.
The system measures the mutation set and downstream effects. When identity or
dependency information is weak, full rebuild and broader validation may be the
honest route.

Repair also preserves the failed artifact for diagnosis while preventing it
from entering the accepted publication surface. History supports learning; it
does not grant failed outputs another path to use.

## Reverse Compilation Is Not Mind Reading

Existing repositories and papers often lack semantic IR. A lifter can extract
files, syntax trees, interfaces, imports, routes, tests, headings, claims,
citations, entities, and explicit constraints into a candidate representation.

Deterministic facts remain distinct from evidence-backed claims and model
guesses. Every lifted node records its origin, exact span or artifact, method,
confidence, parser or model version, rights metadata, and unresolved ambiguity.
An inferred purpose does not become the author's true intent because it is
plausible.

Several historical artifacts can then be compared at stable identities. A
merge bundle preserves source fingerprints, candidate aliases, conflicts,
chosen and rejected alternatives, decision policy, rights constraints, and
trace links. Alias candidates do not merge by name or embedding alone.

This is useful for a living book: papers, project records, source notes, and
chapters can be mined into one architecture without making repeated wording
independent evidence. It also creates copyright, privacy, provenance, and
semantic-laundering risks. Structure can preserve protected expression;
summaries can erase attribution; incompatible claims can be merged into a
false consensus.

Reverse compilation therefore produces a defeasible analysis and an explicit
residual frontier. It is not recovery of one canonical meaning, and
recompilation does not prove that the new artifact is faithful without source-
and target-specific review.

## Failure Cases

**Typed nonsense.** Every field validates, but the source obligation was
misinterpreted.

**Syntax becomes semantics.** Valid HTML, code, JSON, or proof syntax is treated
as preservation of the consumer's meaning.

**Hash equivalence.** Equal or unequal digests are used as a semantic verdict.

**Positional identity.** Inserting one node renames downstream obligations and
breaks repair lineage.

**Silent ambiguity choice.** The compiler selects one plausible reading without
recording alternatives or resolution authority.

**Non-goal loss.** Required exclusions, rights, authority limits, or residual
duties disappear because target generation focuses on positive outputs.

**Role collapse.** A polyadic relation becomes an unordered collection or set
of pairwise edges that loses who did what to whom.

**Dimension error.** Branches, roles, time, evidence, or authority are pooled or
cast because their arrays have compatible shapes.

**Substrate prestige.** A fashionable model, search method, or mathematical
representation is adopted without a consumer-specific advantage test.

**Self-validation.** Generator and validator share the same omission and call
agreement independent evidence.

**Declared local repair.** The receipt names one node while observed mutations
and effects spread beyond its descendants.

**Reverse-compilation laundering.** A model guess becomes a hard constraint,
or several sources become apparent corroboration after provenance is lost.

**Compiler rent.** IR construction, validation, migration, and repair cost more
than direct generation plus competent review.

These failures do not share one fix. Better schemas help with omission, not
interpretation. Stable identity helps repair, not truth. Rich relations help
role preservation, not usefulness. The architecture must be tested end to end.

## The Strongest Simpler Baseline

The strongest baseline is direct generation from the same accepted contract,
followed by the same target validators and a competent reviewer. It receives
the same sources, tools, model budget, repair opportunities, authority, and
outcome horizon. A second baseline uses a structured template or ordinary
workflow without a general semantic IR. Conventional parsers, compilers,
planning languages, retrieval, program synthesis, and human integration are
additional task-appropriate comparators.

The comparison measures obligation and non-goal preservation, ambiguity
handling, role fidelity, invalid acceptance, false rejection, repair locality,
downstream validity, useful artifact quality, latency, compute, human burden,
privacy and rights behavior, migration cost, and residuals. IR quality cannot
be scored only on its own fields.

If direct generation preserves the contract and repairs failures equally well
at lower total cost, explicit compilation should narrow to high-consequence,
repeated, multi-target, or highly repairable work. If a simple template handles
the domain, a universal cognitive language is unnecessary.

## What the Current Work Establishes

The three routed technical owners have bounded but distinct results.

Cognitive Compilation implements three public targets. Its current finite
surface contains 45 live Lean declarations across the retained route module and
the reachable refinement. The refinement validator accepts two fixtures,
rejects four, follows an eight-event obligation, repair, and fresh-validation
lifecycle, and rejects 86 mutations. The trace harness retains two valid and
four expected-invalid compilation records. A separate semantic-preservation
fixture remains blocked and rejects nine mutations.

The QCSA-adjacent implementation produced 2,340 deterministic predictions over
60 synthetic cases, 13 systems, and three seeds, plus one 13-stage reversible
zero-model trace with ten rejecting controls. On that template-generated
workload, the selected full route tied its baseline at 1.000 task accuracy while
using 1.913386 times the operations. The matched-advantage and resource gates
failed. That bounded result does not establish open-domain semantic
preservation or refute question value generally.

Relational Dimension Compilation's finite lifecycle has 42 exact Lean
declarations, eight transitions, 54 exact repairs, seven receipt invalidations,
two non-identifiability results, and three rejecting consumers. It preserves
typed roles and proposal-denominator custody inside the authored model. It does
not establish relational truth, natural higher-order usefulness, efficiency,
irreducibility, or a universal bounded-arity claim.

Mathematical and Search Substrates has a finite adoption surface with 19 exact
Lean declarations, four valid traces, and eight expected-invalid controls. It
checks record and adoption boundaries. No candidate substrate A/B, learned
model, natural workload, kernel benchmark, measured advantage, independent
reproduction, or heterogeneous transfer is established.

None of these results transfers support to the other owners. All three cores
remain `Design rationale` at `argument`. Together they motivate an interface;
they do not demonstrate that the joined compiler preserves meaning or improves
artifacts.

## From a Minimum Compiler to a Cognitive Toolchain

A minimum implementation can compile one accepted publication obligation into
one target page. It needs stable obligation and non-goal identities, an
ambiguity ledger, field lineage, a small semantic IR, one target dialect,
pass/failure receipts, requirement-specific validators, observed repair scope,
dependency-closed rebuild, and retained residuals. Direct generation and a
template workflow provide baselines.

The next experiment should use natural obligations across documents, code,
schemas, proofs, and tool jobs. Gold review must identify outcomes, non-goals,
roles, assumptions, authority, rights, ambiguities, acceptable losses, target
validity, and useful quality. Adversarial cases should insert paraphrase,
omission, role permutation, branch collapse, illegal dimension operations,
authority escape, stale context, evaluator dependence, and repair spillover.

The mature system would expose a family of interoperable dialects rather than
one universal private language. Human contracts, plans, relational state,
documents, programs, experiments, proofs, jobs, and hardware targets would
share stable semantic identities and explicit translation boundaries. Learned,
symbolic, search, database, graph, and solver substrates could compete behind
consumer-specific interfaces.

Every pass would state allowed loss. Every accepted artifact would carry a
translation receipt. Every repair would bind observed mutations. Every
representation or substrate replacement would preserve historical views,
migration residuals, and a fallback path. Unknown meaning would remain unknown
rather than compiled into false precision.

Maturity requires useful advantage over strong direct and structured baselines,
causal ablations, independent semantic and target evaluation, complete costs,
reproduction, and transfer across models, domains, languages, targets,
organizations, ontologies, and hardware. Formal record discipline is necessary
infrastructure, not evidence that this end state exists.

## The Strongest Objection

A semantic IR can become a brittle private language that discards nuance while
presenting an illusion of interoperability. Its types may encode the current
architect's worldview, its validators may reward conformity to that worldview,
and every new domain may require expensive schema work. Direct models may
preserve meaning better through rich context than through forced decomposition.

The objection has force. Explicit structure should activate where stable
identity, multi-target lowering, repair, audit, or consequence justifies it.
The IR must support ambiguity, variants, source expansion, escape hatches, and
schema evolution. Consumers should be able to reject an inadequate dialect or
fall back to the source rather than accept lossy compilation.

Interoperability must be measured through tasks, not declared by shared field
names. Two components can parse the same IR and interpret it differently. A
translation receipt exposes the disagreement surface; it does not remove the
need for tests and qualified judgment.

The architecture should remain plural. Some obligations deserve exact symbolic
forms. Some need relational structures. Some are best handled by direct neural
generation under review. Some require human interpretation. Compilation
coordinates those routes without claiming that one representation captures all
thought.

## Evidence That Would Change the Conclusion

End-to-end systems preserving intent, relational roles, and recovery better
without explicit IR would narrow the compilation boundary. If direct generation
plus target validation matches obligation preservation, ambiguity handling,
repair locality, useful quality, and safety at lower total cost, explicit IR
should be reserved for narrower regimes.

Evidence for the broader architecture would require prospective natural tasks
across several target types, with accepted source semantics, matched direct and
structured baselines, independent target validation, complete failures and
costs, causal ablations of stable identity and lineage, and transfer. Relational
and substrate components would need their own consumer-specific advantage
tests rather than inheriting a compiler win.

A result showing that role-rich or higher-order structure adds no value beyond
competent lower-order rescues would narrow the relational layer. A result
showing that conventional representations dominate proposed substrates would
retire those candidates. The system should preserve the compiler boundary only
where it earns observable value.

## What This Establishes

Cognitive compilation is the discipline of making transformation accountable.
It turns one accepted obligation into a chain of representations whose losses,
ambiguities, validators, repairs, and residuals can be inspected.

The publication artifact failed despite following a valid plan and passing
syntax checks. Semantic identities reveal which privacy and evidence
obligations were lost. Typed relations preserve who approved what and under
which lease. Dimension-safe lowering prevents branch or support scope from
collapsing into actuality. Target validation rejects the concrete page. Repair
changes the addressed nodes and rebuilds their descendants.

None of that proves the compiler understood the source. It creates specific
places where misunderstanding can be found, measured, and corrected. Where a
simpler route performs as well, the compiler should step aside.

Compiled work still depends on exact inputs. The next question is how a system
mounts temporary context, preserves durable knowledge, tracks contradiction and
taint, and forgets what it is no longer allowed to retain. Unit 14 develops
Virtual Context and Durable Semantic Memory as the information boundary beneath
the toolchain.
